# Desktop contracts

`status.json` is generated by the Go status projection and checked byte-for-byte
in Go. Rust checks that its native mapper produces the included views.
TypeScript consumes those exact views to check connection states. Review schema
changes before regenerating with:

```sh
UPDATE_DESKTOP_CONTRACT=1 go test ./internal/quick -run '^TestDesktopSharedStatusContract$'
```

The two `.conf` files contain synthetic, non-secret configuration fixtures.
TypeScript checks exact editor output; Go parses both and verifies that only
the intended first-peer endpoint changed. They cover repeated addresses and
AllowedIPs, IPv6, hooks, routing settings, global transport directives and a
peer-specific FEC directive. Hooks are only parsed, never executed by tests.
